story.iWant: the wiki directory backed up to S3 after each sync operation
story.soThat: knowledge is durably stored and recoverable if the EC2 instance fails

task.title: Create S3 backup script backup-wiki.sh
task.subtask: Create /home/ubuntu/scripts/backup-wiki.sh as a shell script
Accept two arguments: projectId and knowledgeDir (path to the knowledge/ directory)
Construct S3 destination path: s3://futurator-ai-website/knowledge-live/${projectId}/
Execute aws s3 sync ${knowledgeDir} ${s3Path} --delete
The --delete flag ensures articles moved to archive/ or removed are also cleaned from S3
Make script executable (chmod +x)

task.title: Implement error handling and best-effort behavior
task.subtask: Wrap aws s3 sync command in try/catch (|| true in shell) so failures do not propagate
Log errors to stderr: [backup-wiki] ERROR: S3 sync failed for {projectId}: {error}
Log success to stdout: [backup-wiki] Synced {projectId} knowledge to S3 ({n} files uploaded)
Set a timeout of 30 seconds — if sync exceeds this, log warning and continue

task.title: Integrate with graph-sync.mjs
task.subtask: Add S3 backup as a final step in graph-sync.mjs — call backup-wiki.sh after successful Memgraph sync
Alternatively, expose as a standalone callable script that graph-sync.mjs invokes via child_process.exec
Pass projectId and knowledgeDir from graph-sync's existing arguments
Ensure backup failure does not affect graph-sync's exit code (non-blocking)

task.title: Verify IAM permissions
task.subtask: Confirm EC2 IAM role develope-it-ec2-ssm has s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject, s3:ListBucket permissions on futurator-ai-website bucket
Test with aws s3 ls s3://futurator-ai-website/ to verify access
If permissions are missing, document what needs to be added (do not modify IAM directly)

task.title: Validate performance and correctness
task.subtask: Initialize a test project wiki with init-wiki.sh
Run backup-wiki.sh — verify all files appear at s3://futurator-ai-website/knowledge-live/{testProjectId}/
Modify one article and run again — verify only the changed file is uploaded
Measure sync time for incremental change — confirm under 10 seconds
Delete an article locally and run with --delete — verify it is removed from S3
Clean up test data from S3: aws s3 rm --recursive s3://futurator-ai-website/knowledge-live/{testProjectId}/

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: The entire knowledge/ directory is synced to s3://futurator-ai-website/knowledge-live/{projectId}/ after a compilation or sync completes
Only changed files are uploaded (using aws s3 sync differential behavior)
The sync completes in under 10 seconds for typical incremental changes
Errors are logged but do not fail the pipeline (backup is best-effort)
The --delete flag is used so that archived/removed articles are also removed from S3

doc.snippet: D1: Wiki markdown as persistence. D9: Wiki as source of truth, recoverable from S3. Knowledge hierarchy: wiki files (EC2) -> S3 knowledge-live (backup) -> S3 knowledge-archives (versioned) -> Memgraph (query accelerator, rebuilt from wiki).

package.name: aws-cli
package.reason: Uses aws s3 sync command — AWS CLI must be installed on EC2 instance (already present)

constraints.constraint: Story MY-1.3 must be complete — wiki directory structure must exist to have content to back up
Best-effort design — S3 backup must NEVER block or fail the pipeline. Errors logged and swallowed.
EC2 IAM role develope-it-ec2-ssm must have s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject, s3:ListBucket on futurator-ai-website bucket
30-second timeout — if sync exceeds this, log warning and continue (do not block pipeline)
Use --delete flag with aws s3 sync to clean up removed/archived articles from S3
knowledge-live/ path is separate from knowledge-archives/ — live backups are latest-state-only, archives are versioned tarballs
Backup failure must not affect graph-sync.mjs exit code — non-blocking integration
Zero additional infrastructure cost — uses existing S3 bucket and IAM role

interface.name: backup-wiki.sh CLI
interface.details: Arguments: $1=projectId (e.g., spyhunter), $2=knowledgeDir (path to knowledge/ directory). Syncs knowledge/ to s3://futurator-ai-website/knowledge-live/{projectId}/ with --delete flag.

interface.name: AWS S3 Sync
interface.details: aws s3 sync ${knowledgeDir} s3://futurator-ai-website/knowledge-live/${projectId}/ --delete. Differential upload — only changed files transferred. --delete removes files from S3 that are no longer in local source.

interface.name: graph-sync.mjs integration
interface.details: graph-sync.mjs calls backup-wiki.sh as a final step after Memgraph sync completes. Failure is caught and logged but does not affect graph-sync exit code.

standards.standard: S3 sync validation — verify files appear in S3 at correct path after backup
Incremental upload validation — modify one file, verify only that file is transferred
Deletion validation — remove local file, verify --delete flag removes it from S3
Performance validation — measure sync time for incremental changes, confirm under 10 seconds
Error resilience — simulate S3 failure (invalid credentials), verify script exits cleanly with logged error

locations.location: daemon/scripts/graph-sync.mjs (integration point — calls backup-wiki.sh as final step)
